attack_plan.narrative: As the world watches with increasing concern, Russian President Vladimir Putin remains unaccounted for since his last public appearance. The Kremlin, known for its opaque communications, has released a photograph of Putin with U.S. President Obama, but the international community remains skeptical. White smoke has been observed rising above the Kremlin, leading some to speculate that a new leader has taken control. However, other reports suggest Putin is still in charge, possibly under house arrest. The absence of Putin has raised serious concerns about the control of Russian nuclear weapons, a matter of utmost national security. Tanks and armored personnel carriers have been seen moving towards Moscow, scheduled for a military parade marking the one-year anniversary of the Crimea occupation. The Kremlin's reluctance to provide concrete information about Putin’s whereabouts has fueled these fears, especially considering the historical context of power struggles in Russia. With tensions high, the international community awaits further developments.
